title: How to organize the finishing and chemical zone | Workshop
description:
Store paint, glue, stain, and solvent so they stay usable and so they never start a fire.

This is the Finishing and Chemical Zone in the Workshop. About 45-75 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Every product in its original labeled container inside a closed metal cabinet, each lid dated in marker, water based paint on one shelf and solvents and thinners on another. Oily rags in a self-closing metal can with the lid down, a drip tray under the solvent shelf, and no aerosol standing on a sunny sill or near a pilot light.

Shine: Wipe the rim of every can before the lid goes back on, because a rim full of dried finish is why the can skins
Safety: A rag soaked in oil finish generates its own heat as it cures and can ignite with nothing touching it, so it g
Standardize: Date every container with a marker the day it arrives, and write the shelf layout on the inside of the cabinet
Sustain: When you wash out a brush at the end of a finishing job, that is when the can gets its date checked and the ra

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Original containers, dated lids, incompatibles on separate shelves, and rags in a lidded metal can.
